notes.meaning: God announces judgment on Egypt, picturing Himself arriving swiftly like someone riding on a storm cloud. Egypt's false gods cannot protect them and will shake with fear, while the people lose all courage. No human power or idol can stand when the Lord comes to judge.

God says He will stir up civil war across Egypt, turning brothers, neighbors, and cities against each other. Instead of facing an outside army right away, the nation will collapse from its own internal fighting. When people turn against one another, a kingdom quickly destroys itself from within.

The Egyptians will lose their good sense and find their plans ruined by the Lord. In their panic, they will consult idols, fortune-tellers, and spirits of the dead instead of the living God. Looking to false spirits always leaves people empty and without true guidance.

God warns that Egypt will fall under the control of harsh and cruel masters. A fierce foreign king will rule over the land and take away the people's freedom. Losing God's protection leaves a nation exposed to harsh and unfair rulers.

The Nile River, which Egypt depends on for food and trade, will dry up and leave the canals parched and foul-smelling. Without water, the reeds and the crops planted along the riverbanks will wither and blow away in the wind. This disaster shows that the river the Egyptians treated as a god cannot save them from the true Creator.

The fishermen of Egypt will mourn because their livelihood will disappear along with the river waters. Those who fish with hooks in the canals and those who spread nets in the main river will catch nothing. When the river fails, ordinary working people are left with no food to eat and no way to earn a living.

Egypt's famous linen industry will fall apart because the dried-up fields produce no flax to harvest and spin. From the wealthy cloth makers to the hired day laborers, everyone who relies on weaving will be filled with despair. A ruined economy brings hardship to every level of society.

The royal counselors in the ancient city of Zoan boast of their wisdom and royal bloodlines, but their advice is completely foolish. The prophet challenges them to show where their wisdom is now and tell what the Lord of armies has planned against Egypt. Human cleverness cannot match or predict the plans of God.

The leaders of Zoan and Memphis have been thoroughly deceived and are leading their country into ruin. These officials were supposed to be the cornerstones and pillars holding the nation together, but instead they led the people astray. Bad leadership harms everyone who depends on it.

The Lord brings a spirit of confusion and dizziness upon Egypt as a punishment for its pride. The nation stumbles helplessly in all it does, like a drunken man falling in his own mess. Neither the highest leaders nor the lowest workers can find any way to rescue the country.

Egypt's warriors will lose their courage and shake with fear when they see the Lord of armies raise His hand against them. Even the mention of Judah, a smaller neighbor Egypt once looked down on, will cause the Egyptians to tremble. They will realize that Judah's God is carrying out His righteous plans against them.

A great turning point begins as five Egyptian cities start speaking the Hebrew language of God's people and promise loyalty to the Lord. Even a city long known for sun-god worship will abandon its idols and honor the true God. God's grace can reach into the most idol-filled places and transform them.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Ancient copies of Isaiah differ on whether the Hebrew name means City of the Sun or City of Destruction, which was likely a deliberate wordplay on the sun-god worship at Heliopolis.

notes.meaning: True worship will be established openly in Egypt, shown by an altar in the middle of the land and a monument pillar at its border. These visible signs show that the Egyptians will publicly belong to the Lord from one end of their country to the other. Living for God is meant to be seen in all areas of life.

differ.view: The altar is a symbol for the spiritual worship of God in the Christian church, rather than a physical building.
A physical altar will be built in Egypt during a future thousand-year earthly reign of Christ.

notes.meaning: When the Egyptians face cruel mistreatment from enemies, they will cry out to the Lord for help just as Israel once did. God will hear their cries and send them a savior to rescue and defend them. The Lord answers everyone who calls out to Him in their distress.

The Lord will reveal Himself to the Egyptians, and they will truly know and worship Him. They will bring offerings, make solemn vows to God, and faithfully keep their promises. True knowledge of God always leads to sincere and faithful worship.

The Lord will strike Egypt with painful troubles to wake them up, but His purpose is to heal them, not destroy them. When they repent, which means turning away from sin and returning to God, He will hear their prayers and heal their land. God often uses hard times to lead people back to Himself.

A peaceful highway will run between Egypt and Assyria, allowing these two former enemies to travel and trade freely together. Even more remarkably, both nations will put away their weapons and worship the Lord together. God's peace can turn the bitterest enemies into brothers.

Israel will join a three-way partnership with Egypt and Assyria, becoming a channel of blessing to the entire world. The Lord will bless all three equally, giving the Gentiles—people who are not Jewish—the same titles of love once given only to Israel. God's family includes people from every nation who turn to Him in faith.
